summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator and a companion named Tresting enter an office suite where a massacre has occurred. The narrator describes the gruesome scene of disemboweled and tortured victims, including those tied to chairs in a conference room, and the blood-spattered layout. Tresting calls in the scene and identifies the victims through their wallets, while the narrator searches the cubicles and finds the filing cabinets emptied of their paper records.
one_line: Narrator and Tresting discover a bloody massacre in an office suite and find its filing cabinets stripped of records.
key_facts: The narrator and Tresting enter an office suite with weapons drawn, carefully avoiding the soaked carpeting.
A young, sandy-haired man at a computer had been disemboweled.
The women in the next two cubicles looked like they had tried to run; one had her head twisted all the way around.
The men and women in the conference room were older, well-dressed corporate types.
All but one of the conference room victims were tied to their chairs with cloth gags choking their corpses.
The lone untied victim, a middle-aged man, had a .22-inch diameter hole in his forehead.
Tresting handed the narrator a pair of latex gloves and plastic bags to cover their boots.
The narrator says she is not squeamish but closed her eyes briefly at the conference room scene.
Tresting called someone on a Bluetooth earpiece, describing the scene and reading off IDs from wallets he pulled from the victims.
One woman in the conference room had been partially flayed.
The narrator could not deduce anything useful from the blood spatter patterns.
The narrator searched desk drawers and filing cabinets in the outer offices.
Every hanging file folder in the cabinets was empty, and the paper tabs labeling the folders had been pulled.
